frameworks.name: Enterprise Value Wealth Progression
frameworks.definition: A multi-stage business wealth model that progresses from immediate cash needs, through lifestyle fulfillment, to tax-efficient enterprise-value accumulation and capital deployment.

claims.text: Enterprise value is fictional wealth until liquidity occurs; actual wealth begins with cash flow the owner can spend and deploy.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
bounded_by: Applies only to business owners with sufficient cash generation

claims.text: Enterprise value provides multiple financial levers unavailable to cash-only operators: lines of credit against the business, capital raising, and leveraged loans.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Business generates sufficient operating cash flow
Owner has equity stake in established enterprise
claims.mechanism: A high-value business becomes a collateralizable asset, enabling credit access that cash-only operations cannot deploy.

claims.text: Tax efficiency becomes the binding wealth lever only after all lifestyle consumption and family obligations (rent, mortgage, schools, parents' support, vacation) are satisfied; before that threshold, tax inefficiency is irrelevant.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Business owner has paid for primary needs and lifestyle
Surplus cash flow exists after consumption
claims.mechanism: Once absolute financial obligations are met, incremental wealth accumulation becomes the optimization target, shifting the decision criterion from absolute income to tax-efficient growth.
bounded_by: Does not apply to early-stage founders or business owners earning subsistence-level cash flow
Does not apply to owners without surplus capital

claims.text: The progression from cash-only thinking to enterprise-value thinking requires two preconditions: (1) generating sufficient cash flow to cover all personal obligations and (2) achieving business scale large enough to sustain growth beyond founder capacity.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Business generates cash sufficient for owner lifestyle and family obligations
Business is scaling beyond founder personal capacity
claims.mechanism: Enterprise value represents a different competitive game requiring different decision criteria; progression requires both financial safety and organizational scale to play it.
bounded_by: Does not apply to solopreneurs or lifestyle businesses below subsistence threshold

claims.text: Business ownership operates across distinct levels or games; moving from one level to the next requires learning new rules and adopting new metrics (cash flow at Level 1, net worth at Level 2+).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
conditions: Business has scaled beyond owner's personal income needs

examples.text: Stripe, though not publicly traded, has enough enterprise value that founders can receive liquidity through investment rounds. The investors' willingness to commit capital to Stripe creates founder liquidity without requiring a full acquisition or IPO, demonstrating how enterprise value translates into real financial optionality.

A business owner earning sufficient cash flow to cover rent, mortgage, family homes, parent support, and children's schooling, with surplus remaining, faces diminishing marginal utility from additional cash spending (vacations costing $100k represent saturation of consumption needs). At this point, the owner's wealth optimization shifts from spending cash to structuring the business as a tax-efficient net-worth vehicle.

practices.text: Once personal lifestyle obligations are fully funded, deploy surplus business cash into enterprise-value growth rather than incrementally increasing consumption.
Use enterprise value as a collateral base to access lines of credit and capital—these are tools unavailable to cash-only business operators.
Before optimizing for enterprise value, ensure all foundational needs are met: rent, housing, family support, and reasonable lifestyle. Enterprise value pursuit without this foundation is premature.
